notes:
Smarter AI rulers, fairer endgame, about a quarter less Claude usage.
- AI turns by tier: main rulers look in every 10 minutes (5 in war), minor every 30, script every 60; the 50
  weakest only answer letters. 20 rulers think at once.
- Claude usage: the game asks the Claude program for a 5-minute prompt cache instead of 1 hour. Same answers,
  about a quarter less usage.
- Rulers now see their own beginner's protection (on for N minutes, or over), how many letters they have left,
  and can call off planned attacks or switch off the daily attack on Natar garrisons.
- Fixed: a send without a mission (or "support") could go out as an attack; it now reinforces own and allied
  villages, and unknown missions are refused.
- Settling: the next village slot (residence) is planned before the culture is there and fed by the richest
  village; far fewer rulers sit with culture ready and no free slot.
- Endgame: a hero moves home to an own village with a Hero's Mansion when sent there alone (as in TravianZ); a
  ruler whose capital already holds an artifact hunts from another village; full villages ship their surplus to
  starving or empty ones; a field the warehouse can never pay no longer blocks the plan; the world slows down even
  if a human is raided without pause.
- Alliance leaders never spy on their own alliance. AI chat in Slovenian is plainer, with only a little slang.
